Source-assisted reading, F-lmfj, 22 September 2026.
Reader: Codex subagent; exact model identifier unavailable.
Base: review-2026-09-22-image-only.json (unchanged). Assistance: prior F-lmfj report and its candidate; manuscript full views and enlarged crops; 1491 Articella edition image n181. This is not a new independent reading. The edition guides recognition but is not used to fill illegible manuscript text.

Selected manuscript excerpts. Physical lines retain the earlier column numbering: r.a20 is the short separate note before the large-script lemma. Parentheses are proposed abbreviation expansions; [?] marks an uncertain reading; [...] unread text; {above: ...} records an interlinear addition. Letter forms are represented with ordinary u/v characters; this is an expanded reading, not a glyph facsimile. L denotes large-script lemma; C small-script commentary.

r.a24 L u(n)de s(er)mone(m) h(ab)ui in acutis .s. mor-
r.a25 L bis. Dandi cibu(m) s(ecundu)m utile(m) i(n)mutatione(m).
r.a26 L O(portet) a(utem) ut {above: sit} p(er)mutatio sic(ut) p(re)cepi de ea
r.a27 L Dein(de) ut no(n) ministret(ur) aliq(uid)[?] ex sorbitio(n)e
r.a28 L don(ec) dig(er)at(ur) eg(ritu)do. au(t) appareat in
r.b01 L testinis sig(num) p(ro)uocans ad dimitte(n)du(m)
r.b02 L p(ro)hi(bi)tione(m) ab usu sui. (et) ad furie q(uo)q(ue)
r.b03 L signe[?]. [...] appareat a loco q(ui) s(u)b
r.b04 L diafragmate est. sicut dictur(us) sum.

The initial 'in' belonging to intestinis is written at the end of r.a28, not supplied at r.b01. r.b03 also has a tiny interlinear addition above the disputed words, possibly ad; neither its reading nor the corrected construction is resolved. The abbreviation represented signe[?] is not confidently expanded to the edition's significationem. The manuscript reads sui in r.b02, whereas the 1491 lemma has cibi. No emendation is made.

r.b05 C Plurimu(m) a(utem) s(er)monis mei n(on) est n(isi) i(n) p(er)mu-
r.b06 C [...] repletio(n)em (et) euacuatione(m). (et) iuuam(en)tu(m) q(ui)d(em)
r.b07 C [...] cognitio(n)em ei(us) in o(mn)ib(us) eg(ritudini)b(us). (et) fit iuua(mentum)
r.b08 C ip(su)m in eo in q(uo) est s(er)mo m(eu)s .s. in p(er)mut(ati)o(n)e
r.b09 C [...] eg(ritudini)b(us) acutis. ab usu sorbitio(n)is ad uacuit(a)te(m)
r.b10 C uenar(um). O(portet) e(n)i(m) ut sit p(er)mut(ati)o sic(ut) p(re)cepi de eo. De-

The worn starts of r.b06–09 are left uncompleted even though the edition offers intelligible wording. The frozen narrow crop's tellectus/liquam and subsequent uncertain words are superseded here by testinis signum provocans, prohibitionem ab usu sui, etc., on the larger crop and in column context. The frozen record itself is retained unchanged.

Additional commentary check, before the large lemma:
r.a15 C te. (et) h(oc) est t(ra)nq(ui)llitas sto(machi). Q(uonia)m q(ua)n(do) ho(min)is cor(pus)
r.a16 C laborat (et) co(m)edit {above: q(uo)d[?]} [...] g(e)n(er)ant(ur) in
r.a17 C cor(pore) ei(us) h(um)ores m(u)lti. g(ra)uat(ur) (er)g(o) p(ro)p(ter) illos h(um)ores
r.a18 C (et) laborat. (et) labor q(ui)d(em) s(i)g(nifica)t ap(u)d eu(m) in h(oc) loco

r.a16 is not safely read as the earlier report's repeated comedit; the interlinear abbreviation and following baseline words require further work. Do not substitute the print's comedere consuevit for the unclear manuscript sequence.

Further commentary anchor:
r.b16 C Iam agg(re)gauit ipoc(ras) to(tum) s(er)mone(m) suu(m) in h(oc) ser-
r.b17 C mo(n)e in su(m)ma una. (et) p(re)cepit in eo c(uius) disp(ositi)o
r.b18 C est disp(ositi)o una. ut no(n) mutet regi(men) suu(m).

Comparison and result: the 1491 Articella, image n181 (https://archive.org/details/101321207.nlm.nih.gov/page/n181/mode/1up), has the Hec autem lemma and Plurimum autem commentary in the broad right column, the preceding bodily-labour commentary at the far right above, and Iam aggregavit at the far right below. Both text layers agree in sustained distinctive wording. Identify Hippocrates, De regimine acutorum, with Galen's commentary in the medieval Latin Articella form, high confidence. The NLM item metadata explicitly describes De regimine with Galen's commentary.

Important order difference: in the manuscript Oportet ... ab usu sui precedes ad furie quoque ... sicut dicturus sum; the print places ad furie ... sicut dicturus sum before Oportet. Other visible differences include manuscript sui versus printed cibi in the lemma, manuscript de eo versus printed de ea at r.b10, and the absence in manuscript r.b18 of the print's sua after una. These do not justify assigning a translator or recension.

Scope: r_full, v_full, rb1, rb2, va1 and two recto-left tiles were viewed at original detail, as was the edition image. The verso was inspected for condition but not independently collated to a matching edition page. This revision does not verify the old full-leaf transcription, claimed Book II endpoints or 1519 lemma numbers. Cached 1491 and 1519 OCR were searched, but unreliable offsets and unrelated hits added no diagnostic evidence. No attribution is based on a search no-hit. No human palaeographic review occurred.
